builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
summary: The method replaces neural-network and stochastic variational GP classifiers for calibrated pathology prediction by running HMC-based low-rank Gaussian Process Classification on frozen Phikon foundation-model embeddings. It costs the infrastructure to extract embeddings at scale, a low-rank kernel factorization via RPCholesky, and HMC posterior sampling over roughly 300,000 points, which is heavier than a single deterministic classifier and adds implementation and tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen embeddings are mismatched to a target hospital, when kernel or likelihood choices are poorly specified, or when the low-rank approximation discards structure needed for rare subgroups, despite improved reported calibration.
rationale: The paper targets calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift, which matters for production deployment, but the approach depends on specialized GPC machinery and frozen embeddings whose benefits must be validated on the reader's own data and shift conditions before adoption.
technique: Low-rank GPC with HMC on frozen embeddings

claims.statement: The method replaces neural-network and stochastic variational GP classifiers for calibrated pathology prediction by running HMC-based low-rank Gaussian Process Classification on frozen Phikon foundation-model embeddings. It costs the infrastructure to extract embeddings at scale, a low-rank kernel factorization via RPCholesky, and HMC posterior sampling over roughly 300,000 points, which is heavier than a single deterministic classifier and adds implementation and tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen embeddings are mismatched to a target hospital, when kernel or likelihood choices are poorly specified, or when the low-rank approximation discards structure needed for rare subgroups, despite improved reported calibration.
Reduces expected calibration error by up to 88% and false negative rate by up to 90% versus variational GP and neural network baselines, with largest gains under hospital-level distribution shift.
